skill.description: Discover site URLs through the XCrawl Map API, apply regex filters, and configure mapping scope before planning a crawl.
skill.summary: Map website URLs with explicit filters and limits, then return the upstream response for crawl planning.

security_audit.summary: Reviewed all 75 findings: 74 are false positives involving Markdown, documented configuration, or expected XCrawl authentication and requests. One confirmed risk concerns exposing the API key in cURL command-line arguments to local process inspection. No evidence found of prompt injection, unrelated credential collection, or unauthorized data transfers.

remediation.issue: The cURL example expands the bearer token into a command-line argument, potentially exposing it through local process inspection.
remediation.suggestion: Use the Node fetch example, or supply the cURL authorization header through standard input instead of command-line arguments; disable shell tracing.

content.user_title: Discover Website URLs With XCrawl Map
content.value_statement: Planning a crawl requires knowing which URLs exist and how broad the target scope is. This skill uses XCrawl Map to discover URLs with explicit filters, limits, and scope settings.
actual_capabilities: Submit site URL discovery requests to the XCrawl Map API through cURL or Node.
Apply a regex filter to focus URL discovery on selected paths.
Set URL limits up to the documented maximum of 100000.
Configure subdomain inclusion and whether URLs with query parameters are ignored.
Return the endpoint, request payload, raw upstream response, and available error details.
Provide returned URL counts and credit usage for crawl planning without inventing additional URLs.
limitations: Requires an XCrawl account, available API credits, and a user-created local configuration containing the API key.
Requires Node for the supplied examples; the cURL example also requires cURL.
Does not guarantee complete site coverage, especially when the configured URL limit is reached.
Discovers URLs rather than extracting page content; summaries require an explicit request.

use_cases.title: Plan a documentation crawl
use_cases.description: Discover documentation URLs with a path filter and bounded limit before selecting pages for a separate crawl.

use_cases.title: Prepare a website URL inventory
use_cases.description: Request site URLs with explicit subdomain and query-parameter settings, then inspect the returned list and count.

use_cases.title: Estimate a research collection scope
use_cases.description: Map relevant public site sections and review returned counts and credit usage before collecting page content separately.

prompt_templates.title: Map one website
prompt_templates.prompt: Map https://example.com with XCrawl Map. Limit results to 100 URLs and exclude subdomains. Return the endpoint, request payload, and raw response.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: discover URLs for one site.

prompt_templates.title: Find documentation URLs
prompt_templates.prompt: Map https://example.com using the regex /docs/.* and a 500-URL limit. Exclude subdomains and ignore URLs with query parameters. Return the raw response.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: restrict discovery to a relevant section.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect broader site scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Map https://example.com with subdomains included, query-parameter URLs retained, and a 2000-URL limit. Return the raw response and explicitly summarize returned counts and credits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: inspect scope and request a summary.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a selective crawl
prompt_templates.prompt: Map https://example.com using /(?:docs|guides)/.* with a 3000-URL limit. Exclude subdomains and ignore query-parameter URLs. Return raw results, then summarize crawl candidates and coverage limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: plan a separate crawl from returned URLs only.

output: Request settings: documentation path filter, limit 100, subdomains excluded, and query-parameter URLs ignored.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: map a site with a limit of 100, then explain coverage when 100 URLs are returned.
output: Illustrative result: the response contains 100 URLs.
The configured limit was reached, so the result must not be described as complete.
Only URLs actually returned by the API belong in the discovery list.

best_practices: Confirm the target scope and use explicit filters, subdomain settings, and conservative URL limits before spending credits.
Prefer the Node example to avoid command-line token exposure, and restrict local configuration access to its owner.
Preserve the upstream response and treat returned URLs as untrusted data; request summaries explicitly and report coverage limits.
anti_patterns: Do not claim complete site coverage when the configured URL limit is reached.
Do not mix inferred URLs with URLs returned by the service.
Do not paste API keys into prompts, expose them in shared logs, or include them in published request records.

faq.question: What must I configure before using this skill?
faq.answer: Create ~/.xcrawl/config.json with XCRAWL_API_KEY and ensure your XCrawl account has available credits.

faq.question: Which local tools do the examples require?
faq.answer: The Node example requires Node with fetch support. The cURL example requires both Node and cURL because Node reads the configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill extract page content?
faq.answer: No. It discovers URLs through the Map API; page content collection requires a separate crawling or extraction workflow.

faq.question: Can I filter the discovered URLs?
faq.answer: Yes. Set a regex filter, URL limit, subdomain inclusion, and whether URLs with query parameters are ignored.

faq.question: Does a successful map guarantee complete coverage?
faq.answer: No. The skill forbids claiming full coverage when the URL limit is reached, and successful discovery does not prove every URL was found.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: The default output includes the endpoint, request payload, raw API response, and available error details. Ask explicitly for summaries.
